title: US chip stocks post longest losing streak since 2008
source_used: Capital Brief (summarising Bloomberg, Reuters and WSJ); BigGo Finance for cross-check
key_facts: Capital Brief, 17 Oct: chip stocks fell for an eighth consecutive session on Friday, their longest losing streak since 2008.
Broadcom fell 4.5% and an index of semiconductor stocks 3.8%.
The Nasdaq fell 2.1% on Friday and 4.5% over the week; the S&P 500 fell 1.1% on Friday and 2% on the week.
CoreWeave fell another 11.9%, bringing its five-day loss to nearly 25%.
Energy stocks in the S&P 500 gained 2.5% and utilities 1.4% as investors rotated out of tech.
Capital Brief cites Bloomberg, Reuters and WSJ; Reuters (C07-01) separately describes the chip index as on track for an eighth straight daily decline.

BigGo Finance says the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.83% on 16 Oct, about 22% below its 22 June record, and cites Barron's for the SOXX chip ETF's nine-session losing streak, its longest since May 2006.
quote_evidence: Chip stocks fell for an eighth consecutive session, their longest losing streak since 2008.
Energy stocks in the S&P 500 gained 2.5%, while utilities rallied 1.4%.
Neocloud CoreWeave continued to slide as investors worried about how it would finance its data centres amid rising borrowing costs.
why_it_matters_hint: The sell-off in chip stocks has now run for eight straight sessions and is pulling the wider market down.
